column1: # Phase 0 clip set. The .safetensors are gitignored, so this file plus the .txt prompts is what
# makes the set reconstructible — the ledger records only the clip NAME.
# 29 pixel frames at 24 fps from --start 0) and NAME_te.safetensors (encode_text.py on NAME.txt).
# The probe truncates to latent_t=7; the VAE is temporally causal, so the first 7 latent frames
# Prompts are written to match the first 29 frames only, which is all the probe sees. They are
# Context-IR, not the corpus's own .txt captions — those are short free-form generation prompts
# and pairing one with the DiT would be off-distribution in prompt space.
# Selected for spread over camera motion (static / push / pull / arc / tracking), subject count
# (0, 1, 2) and render style (2D pixel, pixel-rig on white, photoreal miniature, live-action).
# The `untagged` corpus category is excluded deliberately.
# Second temporal windows (start=2.5s, same 29 frames @ 24 fps). Same source video and the same
# text embedding as the base name — more motion variety without reloading the 32B text encoder.
# Geometry control. Same source, same 29-frame window, same prompt as `isodiorama` — only --size
# differs (640 640, so 40x40 latent and 2800 video tokens against 512's 32x32 and 1792). The first
# three ledger rows all sat at 512x512 latent_t=7, so their agreement was measured over content
# while geometry stayed fixed; this row is the one that varies geometry instead. Its _te file is a
# byte copy of isodiorama's, which is the point: the text side must not move.
